summary: Priyanka Pradeep Salekar works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. She earned a B.A. from the University of Mumbai (2014-2017) and an M.A. from Deccan College (2017-2019), later becoming a PhD Researcher and Teaching Assistant at IIT Bombay in 2021.

Priyanka Sharma, who works in Indology and other fields, completed an M.Phil at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya (2011-2012). She served as an Assistant Professor at Lovely Professional University from 2018 to 2019.

Priyanku Chakraborty works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. Supervised by Aishwarya Biswas, Chakraborty held a post at The Asiatic Society in 2022 and served as the Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies there (attested 2026).
Priya Vrat Sharma (1920-2008) worked in the fields of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Director at Banaras Hindu University and at its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø, a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, studied at Oslo, the Sorbonne under Georg Morgenstierne, and Mainz. He held posts at Mainz, Columbia, and Harvard, where he was Aga Khan Professor (~1991-2015).

Prudence R. Myer (1920-2001) was an art historian working in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. from NYU's Institute of Fine Arts, she taught at Mount Holyoke (1956), Tulane (1959-1963), and UC Santa Barbara (1966-1968).
Przemysław Szczurek is an Indologist who has held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and at the University of Breslau, where he served as Professor of Indology around 2005.

Puji Sulani specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed an M.Pd. at the State University of Jakarta (2012-2014) and a doctorate at the University of Indonesia (2018-2023), and joined Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Negeri Sriwijaya in 2009.
Pulinbihari Chakravarti worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).
Punyavijaya (1895-1971) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Purna Harsha Bajracharya worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. By 1972, Bajracharya served as Chief Research Officer at both the Department of Archaeology and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Purnima Dhavan is a historian of South Asia and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia before holding posts at Bowdoin College (2002-2003), St. John's University (2003-2005), and the University of Washington (2005).

Purushottam Mahadev Joshi (1904-1989) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935-1947) and served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894-1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Harvard, and held posts at Fergusson College (1932), Visva-Bharati University (1945-1948), and the University of Delhi (1957-1960).

Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and earned a PhD from La Trobe University. He held posts at Deakin, Melbourne, UC Berkeley, Stony Brook, and Columbia.

Pushpendra Kumar (b. 1936) is an Indologist who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 1976) and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891-1973) worked in Indology and other fields. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and as president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Kyaw completed a PhD at King's College London in 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Pál Büchler (1877-1946) worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. from Eötvös Loránd University, where he studied from around 1897 to 1907, and later served as a professor at the Commercial School in Târgu-Mureș (1926-1930).

Péter-Dániel Szántó specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Merton College, Hamburg, All Souls College, Leiden, and Eötvös Loránd University.
